716	    def release_record_with_dependencies(self, version, checklist, template,
717	                                         rollback, dependencies):
718	        # Read-only release snapshot that additionally freezes the dependency
719	        # map: the audit follows audit_checklist and the dependency report
720	        # follows check_dependencies exactly, and the record is built only
721	        # when both reports are ready. An unfinished optional item never
722	        # blocks the record by itself, but as a direct or indirect
723	        # prerequisite of a required item it blocks through the existing
724	        # effective-status propagation. The returned snapshot is detached
725	        # from every passed object and carries no generated timestamp, so
726	        # identical inputs yield identical records.
727	        audit = self.audit_checklist(version, checklist, template)
728	        dependency_check = self.check_dependencies(version, checklist, dependencies)
729	        if not audit["ready"] or not dependency_check["ready"]:

731	        target_version, steps = self._validated_rollback(rollback, version)
732	        items = self._validated_checklist(checklist, version)
733	        prerequisites = self._validated_dependencies(
734	            dependencies, {item["id"] for item in items})
735	        # Every normalized checklist id appears in checklist order; an
736	        # undeclared item freezes to an empty array and declared
737	        # prerequisites keep their dependency-array order.
738	        frozen = {item["id"]: list(prerequisites.get(item["id"], ())) for item in items}
739	        changes = self.export_releases([version])[version]
740	        return {"version": version,
741	                "changes": copy.deepcopy(changes),
742	                "notes": self.notes(version),
743	                "audit": copy.deepcopy(audit),
744	                "rollback": {"targetVersion": target_version, "steps": steps},
745	                "dependencies": frozen,
746	                "dependencyCheck": copy.deepcopy(dependency_check)}

748	    def _validated_rollback(self, rollback, release_version):
749	        # Validate the rollback plan: a strict {"targetVersion", "steps"}
750	        # object. targetVersion is null or a registered version numerically
751	        # smaller than the release; steps is a non-empty array of single-line
752	        # strings, stored trimmed with order and duplicates preserved.
753	        if not isinstance(rollback, dict):
754	            raise ValueError("rollback plan must be a JSON object")
755	        if set(rollback) != {"targetVersion", "steps"}:
756	            raise ValueError("rollback plan requires exactly targetVersion and steps")
757	        target_version = rollback["targetVersion"]
758	        if target_version is not None:
759	            if not isinstance(target_version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, target_version):
760	                raise ValueError("rollback targetVersion must be null or a valid version")
761	            records = self._read_store()
762	            if target_version not in records:
763	                raise ValueError("rollback targetVersion must be a registered release")
764	            if _version_order(target_version) >= _version_order(release_version):
765	                raise ValueError("rollback targetVersion must be smaller than the release version")
766	        steps = rollback["steps"]
767	        if not isinstance(steps, list) or not steps:
768	            raise ValueError("rollback steps must be a non-empty array of strings")
769	        normalized = []
770	        for step in steps:
771	            if not isinstance(step, str) or "\n" in step or "\r" in step or not step.strip():
772	                raise ValueError("rollback steps must be non-empty single-line strings")
773	            normalized.append(step.strip())
774	        return target_version, normalized

776	    def reconcile_checklist(self, version, checklist, template):
777	        # Read-only update of a same-version checklist against a revised
778	        # template: unchanged definitions keep their status, redefined items
779	        # reset to pending, new items are added and inapplicable items drop.
780	        if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
781	            raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
782	        items = self._validated_checklist(checklist, version)
783	        template_items = self._validated_template(template)
784	        # The whole store is validated before the version is looked up.
785	        records = self._read_store()
786	        if version not in records:
787	            raise ValueError("unknown release")
788	        selected = self._applicable_template_items(template_items, records[version])
789	        # Ids match case-sensitively after trimming, without Unicode normalization.
790	        previous = {item["id"]: item for item in items}
791	        reconciled, retained, reset, added = [], [], [], []
792	        for expected in selected:
793	            item_id = expected["id"]
794	            actual = previous.get(item_id)
795	            if actual is None:
796	                reconciled.append(dict(expected))
797	                added.append(item_id)
798	            elif actual["text"] != expected["text"] or actual["required"] != expected["required"]:
799	                # A redefined item takes the new definition and returns to pending.
800	                reconciled.append(dict(expected))
801	                reset.append(item_id)
802	            else:
803	                reconciled.append({"id": item_id, "text": expected["text"],
804	                                   "required": expected["required"], "status": actual["status"]})
805	                retained.append(item_id)
806	        selected_ids = {item["id"] for item in selected}
807	        removed = [item["id"] for item in items if item["id"] not in selected_ids]
808	        return {"version": version, "items": reconciled,
809	                "retained": retained, "reset": reset, "added": added, "removed": removed}

811	    def migrate_checklist(self, base_version, target_version, checklist, template):
812	        # Read-only cross-version migration: only progress still backed by the
813	        # target release is inherited. Unlike reconcile_checklist, a same-id
814	        # item whose definition is unchanged keeps its status solely when the
815	        # change entries covered by the item's template categories are
816	        # identical between the two registered releases.
817	        for version in (base_version, target_version):
818	            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
819	                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
820	        # The checklist is validated against the base version it declares; the
821	        # template is validated in full before the target filter is applied.
822	        items = self._validated_checklist(checklist, base_version)
823	        template_items = self._validated_template(template)
824	        # The whole store is validated before either version is looked up.
825	        records = self._read_store()
826	        if base_version not in records:
827	            raise ValueError("unknown release")
828	        if target_version not in records:
829	            raise ValueError("unknown release")
830	        selected = self._applicable_template_items(template_items, records[target_version])
831	        # Reuse the diff classification as the change comparison; the scope
832	        # filters it down to the categories a template item declares. When the
833	        # item declares none every category is compared, categories not present
834	        # in the target release included.
835	        added, removed, unchanged = self._diff_entries(
836	            self._clean_changes(records[base_version]),
837	            self._clean_changes(records[target_version]))
838	        changed_by_category = {}
839	        for category in CATEGORIES:
840	            changed_by_category[category] = any(
841	                entry["category"] == category for entry in added + removed)
842	        previous = {item["id"]: item for item in items}
843	        definitions = {item["id"]: item for item in template_items}
844	        migrated, retained, reset, added_ids = [], [], [], []
845	        for expected in selected:
846	            item_id = expected["id"]
847	            actual = previous.get(item_id)
848	            if actual is None:
849	                migrated.append(dict(expected))
850	                added_ids.append(item_id)
851	            elif actual["text"] != expected["text"] or actual["required"] != expected["required"]:
852	                migrated.append(dict(expected))
853	                reset.append(item_id)
854	            else:
855	                categories = definitions[item_id]["categories"]
856	                scope = CATEGORIES if categories is None else tuple(categories)
857	                if all(not changed_by_category[category] for category in scope):
858	                    migrated.append({"id": item_id, "text": expected["text"],
859	                                     "required": expected["required"], "status": actual["status"]})
860	                    retained.append(item_id)
861	                else:
862	                    migrated.append(dict(expected))
863	                    reset.append(item_id)
864	        selected_ids = {item["id"] for item in selected}
865	        removed_ids = [item["id"] for item in items if item["id"] not in selected_ids]
866	        return {"baseVersion": base_version, "version": target_version,
867	                "items": migrated,
868	                "retained": retained, "reset": reset, "added": added_ids,
869	                "removed": removed_ids}

871	    def update_checklist(self, version, updates, checklist_path):
872	        # Batch-update the statuses of a local checklist file after confirming
873	        # every expected status still matches the read bytes: one mismatch
874	        # rejects the whole batch. Only when at least one status changes is the

882	        # whose target status would not change anything.

884	            actual = status_by_id.get(item_id)

886	                raise ValueError("update item id must exist in the checklist")
887	            if actual != expected:

893	                                 ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
894	            _atomic_write(path, content)
895	        ready = all(item["status"] == "done" for item in resulting if item["required"])

897	                "updated": updated, "ready": ready}

903	        # order instead of raised, and nothing is ever written.

908	        # status is already satisfied; conflicts keep the updates-array order.

923	            updated = []
924	            changed = False
925	        else:
926	            can_update = True
927	            updated, resulting = self._apply_checklist_updates(items, normalized_updates)

938	        # from any present item). An incoming side equal to the base or to the
939	        # current side keeps the current side; otherwise a current side equal
940	        # to the base adopts the incoming side; anything else is one whole-item
941	        # conflict that keeps the current presence state and content.

943	            version, base, incoming, current)

954	    def resolve_merge_checklist(self, version, base, incoming, current, decisions):
955	        # Read-only confirmation layer over preview_merge_checklist: decisions
956	        # maps original preview conflict ids to "incoming" or "current"; empty
957	        # and partial maps are allowed. A chosen side is adopted as one whole
958	        # item and choosing a side that lacks the id deletes the item.
959	        # Unchosen conflicts keep their original details and the current side.

1519	                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")

1521	        _validated_config(target_config)
1522	        _validated_config(expected_config)
1523	        choices = _validated_decisions(decisions)
1524	        # The whole store is validated before either version is looked up.
1525	        records = self._read_store()
1526	        if base_version not in records:
1527	            raise ValueError("unknown release")
1528	        if target_version not in records:
1529	            raise ValueError("unknown release")

1531	        if path.is_symlink():
1532	            raise ValueError("current configuration file must not be a symbolic link")
1533	        if _same_file(self.path, path):
1534	            raise ValueError("current configuration file must not be the same file as the store")

1536	        try:

1547	        conflicts = []
1548	        _preview_config_values(base_config, target_config, current_config, "", conflicts)
1549	        conflict_paths = {entry["path"] for entry in conflicts}
1550	        for decision_path in choices:

1553	        resolved = []
1554	        config = _resolve_config_values(
1555	            base_config, target_config, current_config, "", choices, resolved)
1556	        chosen_paths = {entry["path"] for entry in resolved}
1557	        if any(entry["path"] not in chosen_paths for entry in conflicts):

    @staticmethod
    def _clean_changes(changes):
        if not isinstance(changes, list) or not changes:
            raise ValueError("at least one change is required")
        clean = []
        for change in changes:
            if not isinstance(change, dict):
                raise ValueError("changes require a valid category and single-line text")
            category, text = change.get("category"), change.get("text")
            if category not in CATEGORIES or not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip() or "\n" in text or "\r" in text:
                raise ValueError("changes require a valid category and single-line text")
            clean.append({"category": category, "text": text.strip()})
        return clean

    def _validated_payload(self, payload):
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            raise ValueError("import payload must be a JSON object")
        normalized = {}
        for version, changes in payload.items():
            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
            normalized[version] = self._clean_changes(changes)
        return normalized

    def _read_store(self):
        if not self.path.exists():
            return {}
        # OSErrors (directory target, permissions, ...) propagate unchanged.
        raw = self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        if not raw:
            raise ValueError("release store must be a JSON object")
        try:
            records = _loads_unique(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise ValueError("release store must be a JSON object") from exc
        return self._validated_records(records)

    @staticmethod
    def _validated_records(records):
        if not isinstance(records, dict):
            raise ValueError("release store must be a JSON object")
        for version, changes in records.items():
            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
            # Validates without replacing: whitespace, extra fields and order survive.
            ReleaseDesk._clean_changes(changes)
        return records

    def _write_store(self, records):
        content = json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
        _atomic_write(self.path, content)

    def versions(self):
        records = self._read_store()
        return sorted(records, key=lambda version: tuple(map(int, version.split("."))))

    def notes(self, version):
        records = self._read_store()
        if version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        lines = [f"# {version}"]
        for category in CATEGORIES:
            changes = [change["text"] for change in records[version] if change["category"] == category]
            if changes:
                lines.extend(["", f"## {category}", *[f"- {text}" for text in changes]])
        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

    def diff(self, base_version, target_version):
        for version in (base_version, target_version):
            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        records = self._read_store()
        base = self._checked_entries(records, base_version)
        target = self._checked_entries(records, target_version)
        added, removed, unchanged = self._diff_entries(base, target)
        return {"baseVersion": base_version, "targetVersion": target_version,
                "added": added, "removed": removed, "unchanged": unchanged}

    @staticmethod
    def _diff_entries(base, target):
        # Classify cleaned entries of target relative to base, per category in
        # fixed order; duplicates pair up by occurrence within each category.
        added, removed, unchanged = [], [], []
        for category in CATEGORIES:
            base_entries = [entry for entry in base if entry["category"] == category]
            target_entries = [entry for entry in target if entry["category"] == category]
            available = Counter(entry["text"] for entry in base_entries)
            for entry in target_entries:
                if available[entry["text"]] > 0:
                    available[entry["text"]] -= 1
                    unchanged.append(entry)
                else:
                    added.append(entry)
            matched = Counter(entry["text"] for entry in target_entries)
            for entry in base_entries:
                if matched[entry["text"]] > 0:
                    matched[entry["text"]] -= 1
                else:
                    removed.append(entry)
        return added, removed, unchanged

    @staticmethod
    def _checked_entries(records, version):
        if version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        return ReleaseDesk._clean_changes(records[version])

    def diff_config(self, base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config):
        # Read-only structural comparison of two externally supplied
        # configurations for two registered versions. Nothing is stored and
        # the configurations are never inferred from change entries.
        for version in (base_version, target_version):
            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        _validated_config(base_config)
        _validated_config(target_config)
        # The whole store is validated before either version is looked up.
        records = self._read_store()
        if base_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        if target_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        added, removed, changed = [], [], []
        _diff_config_values(base_config, target_config, "", added, removed, changed)
        # Paths sort by Unicode code point, not by locale.
        added.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        removed.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        changed.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        return {"baseVersion": base_version, "targetVersion": target_version,
                "added": added, "removed": removed, "changed": changed}

    def preview_config(self, base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config, current_config):
        # Read-only three-way preview of applying the base->target plan onto
        # the current configuration. Nothing is stored and the configurations
        # are never inferred from change entries.
        for version in (base_version, target_version):
            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        _validated_config(base_config)
        _validated_config(target_config)
        _validated_config(current_config)
        # The whole store is validated before either version is looked up.
        records = self._read_store()
        if base_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        if target_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        conflicts = []
        preview = _preview_config_values(base_config, target_config, current_config, "", conflicts)
        # Paths sort by Unicode code point, not by locale.
        conflicts.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        return {"baseVersion": base_version, "targetVersion": target_version,
                "canApply": not conflicts, "config": preview, "conflicts": conflicts}

    def resolve_config(self, base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config,
                       current_config, decisions):
        # Read-only three-way resolution with per-path conflict choices. The
        # decisions map original preview_config conflict paths verbatim to
        # "target", "current" or a custom {"present", "value"?} decision;
        # nothing is stored or inferred from entries.
        for version in (base_version, target_version):
            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        _validated_config(base_config)
        _validated_config(target_config)
        _validated_config(current_config)
        choices = _validated_decisions(decisions)
        # The whole store is validated before either version is looked up.
        records = self._read_store()
        if base_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        if target_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        conflicts = []
        _preview_config_values(base_config, target_config, current_config, "", conflicts)
        conflict_paths = {entry["path"] for entry in conflicts}
        # Keys match the original conflict paths verbatim, using the same JSON
        # Pointer escaping: no trimming, normalization or subpath selection.
        for path in choices:
            if path not in conflict_paths:
                raise ValueError("decision path is not a conflict path")
        resolved = []
        config = _resolve_config_values(
            base_config, target_config, current_config, "", choices, resolved)
        chosen_paths = {entry["path"] for entry in resolved}
        remaining = [entry for entry in conflicts if entry["path"] not in chosen_paths]
        # Paths sort by Unicode code point, not by locale.
        remaining.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        resolved.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        return {"baseVersion": base_version, "targetVersion": target_version,
                "canApply": not remaining, "config": config,
                "conflicts": remaining, "resolved": resolved}

    def apply_config(self, base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config,
                     expected_config, decisions, current_path):
        # Applying a confirmed plan to a local configuration file: the file is
        # read, checked against the expected snapshot, resolved exactly like
        # resolve_config and, only when the result differs, replaced wholesale
        # with UTF-8 JSON ending in a newline. Nothing else is modified.
        for version in (base_version, target_version):
            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        _validated_config(base_config)
        _validated_config(target_config)
        _validated_config(expected_config)
        choices = _validated_decisions(decisions)
        # The whole store is validated before either version is looked up.
        records = self._read_store()
        if base_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        if target_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        path = Path(current_path)
        if path.is_symlink():
            raise ValueError("current configuration file must not be a symbolic link")
        if _same_file(self.path, path):
            raise ValueError("current configuration file must not be the same file as the store")
        # A missing target or an unreadable file raises OSError unchanged.
        try:
            raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
            raise ValueError("current configuration file must contain UTF-8 encoded JSON") from exc
        try:
            current_config = _loads_unique(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise ValueError("current configuration file must contain UTF-8 encoded JSON") from exc
        _validated_config(current_config)
        if not _json_values_equal(expected_config, current_config):
            raise ValueError("current configuration does not match the expected configuration")
        conflicts = []
        _preview_config_values(base_config, target_config, current_config, "", conflicts)
        conflict_paths = {entry["path"] for entry in conflicts}
        for decision_path in choices:
            if decision_path not in conflict_paths:
                raise ValueError("decision path is not a conflict path")
        resolved = []
        config = _resolve_config_values(
            base_config, target_config, current_config, "", choices, resolved)
        chosen_paths = {entry["path"] for entry in resolved}
        if any(entry["path"] not in chosen_paths for entry in conflicts):
            raise ValueError("unresolved conflicts remain")
        # Paths sort by Unicode code point, not by locale.
        resolved.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        changed = not _json_values_equal(config, current_config)
        if changed:
            content = json.dumps(config, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
            _atomic_write(path, content)
        return {"baseVersion": base_version, "targetVersion": target_version,
                "changed": changed, "config": config, "resolved": resolved}

content.content:
1	# Release Desk
2	
3	Maintain local release records and generate Markdown notes grouped as Added, Changed and Fixed. Requires Python 3.10+; only the standard library is used.
4	
5	`python3 release_desk.py notes 1.1.0` renders the included second release. `python3 release_desk.py versions` lists sample versions in numeric order. `samples/next-changes.json` is a candidate change list; to try registration without changing the sample store, use `python3 release_desk.py --store .state/releases.json add 1.2.0 samples/next-changes.json` and query that same store.
6	
7	Version identifiers have exactly three nonnegative numeric components, without prefixes, prerelease suffixes or leading zeros. Each release has at least one single-line change with a recognized category. Existing versions cannot be replaced. Category order is fixed and the input order within a category is retained. This version does not inspect Git or publish packages.
8	
9	`python3 release_desk.py diff 1.0.0 1.1.0` compares two registered versions in the same store and prints a single-line JSON object with `baseVersion`, `targetVersion` and the `added`, `removed` and `unchanged` entries of the target relative to the base. Entries match on category plus trimmed, case-sensitive text; duplicates pair up by occurrence. Comparing a version with itself or a higher with a lower version is allowed. The comparison is read-only and never infers actual product changes.
10	
11	`ReleaseDesk.diff_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config)` is a read-only structural comparison of two externally supplied JSON configuration objects, and `python3 release_desk.py diff-config 1.0.0 1.1.0 base.json target.json` reads both configurations from UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); comparing a version with itself or a higher with a lower version is allowed. The configurations come solely from the arguments or files — they are never written to the store and never inferred from change entries — and neither the passed objects, the files nor the store are modified, and no directory is created.
12	
13	Each root configuration must be a JSON object. When the same field exists in both and both values are objects, comparison descends recursively; otherwise the complete values are compared. Arrays are never split: they compare as whole values and element order is significant, with objects inside arrays following the same object rules. A field or whole subobject present only in the target yields one `added` entry, one present only in the base yields one `removed` entry, both carrying `path` and `value`; a field present on both sides with differing values yields a `changed` entry carrying `path`, `before` (the base value) and `after` (the target value). All three arrays are always present, and identical configurations return three empty arrays. `path` is a JSON Pointer rooted at the empty string (`/a/b`, `/` for an empty field name), with `~` and `/` in field names escaped as `~0` and `~1`. Each array is sorted by path in Unicode code point order; key matching is case-sensitive with no Unicode normalization and empty key names are allowed. Booleans differ from numbers even when comparing `true` with `1`, numerically equal integers and floats compare equal, `null` differs from a missing field, and object key order is ignored.
14	
15	An invalid or unknown version, invalid store content, a non-object root, a non-string key, a non-JSON value (including non-finite numbers) or a circular reference raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects encoding errors, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level (the same whole-file duplicate-key rule as everywhere), printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2 for any of these and the single-line result with exit 0 on success. A missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown.
16	
17	`ReleaseDesk.preview_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config, current_config)` is a read-only three-way preview that checks whether applying the base→target plan would overwrite independent edits already present in the current configuration, and `python3 release_desk.py preview-config 1.0.0 2.0.0 base.json target.json current.json` reads all three configurations from UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); same-version and reverse-order pairs are allowed, just like `diff-config`. The configurations come solely from the arguments or files and follow the same validation, equality, pointer and key rules as `diff_config`, and nothing — the passed objects, the files, the store — is modified and no directory is created.
18	
19	For each field, the plan is the base→target change. A field the plan does not change keeps its current presence state and value, including independent current edits and current-only fields. When the plan does change a field, a current value equal to the target is kept, a current state equal to the base adopts the target (whole additions and deletions included), and any other state is resolved field by field only when the field exists on all three sides and all three values are objects; otherwise it is one conflict at that path whose preview keeps the current field's presence state and value. Whole subobject additions and deletions, arrays (never split) and type changes are always judged as a whole, so a whole-value conflict never lists subpaths; every other non-conflicting change still enters the preview. Equality uses the `diff_config` rules, including `null` differing from a missing field and two missing fields being equal. The result holds only `baseVersion`, `targetVersion`, `canApply`, `config` and `conflicts`: `config` is the complete previewed object, `canApply` is true only when `conflicts` is empty, and each conflict holds only `path` plus `base`, `target` and `current`, each of those holding a `present` boolean and a `value` only when present. `path` uses the same JSON Pointer escaping as `diff-config`, and `conflicts` is sorted by path in Unicode code point order. For example, a target that changes the port while the current config only changes a timeout keeps both changes, while both sides changing the same port to different values keeps the current port and reports a `/port` conflict.
20	
21	An invalid or unknown version, invalid store or a configuration violating the existing config validation rules raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects encoding errors, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the three files, printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid preview prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when it reports conflicts, and a missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown. Neither success nor failure modifies the arguments, the input files or the store, or creates any file or directory.
22	
23	`ReleaseDesk.resolve_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config, current_config, decisions)` is a read-only confirmation layer over `preview_config`, and `python3 release_desk.py resolve-config 1.0.0 2.0.0 base.json target.json current.json decisions.json` reads the three configurations and the decisions from four UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); same-version and reverse-order pairs are allowed, and the configurations come solely from the arguments or files under the same validation, equality, pointer and key rules as `preview_config`. `decisions` is a JSON object, possibly empty, mapping original `preview_config` conflict paths to either the string `"target"`, the string `"current"` or a custom decision object; strings and custom objects may be mixed freely in the same map. Keys match verbatim using the same JSON Pointer escaping (`~0`, `~1`), with no trimming or Unicode normalization; only whole conflict paths are accepted — arrays, type changes and whole-object conflicts cannot be decided at subpaths, and non-conflict fields are rejected — and partial selections are allowed. Choosing `"target"` adopts that conflict's complete target-side presence state and value; choosing `"current"` keeps the current side and records the conflict as handled. When the chosen side is missing the field is deleted, and a `null` side value is kept as a value rather than treated as missing. Every other non-conflicting change and every independent current edit keeps its preview result.
24	
25	A custom decision object holds a strict boolean `present`. When `present` is true the object holds exactly `present` and a required `value`; when `present` is false it holds exactly `present` and the field is deleted. `value` accepts any legal JSON value, including `null`, arrays and objects. The custom value replaces the selected field wholesale: objects, arrays and type changes are never recursively merged, and a value numerically or structurally equal to the target or current side still counts as a custom, handled decision. Every other non-conflicting change and every independent current edit keeps its preview result. For example, when the port is 80 on the base side, 8080 on the target side and 9000 on the current side, a `{"present": true, "value": 9001}` decision on `/port` confirms 9001 while an independently modified timeout keeps its current value.
26	
27	The result holds only `baseVersion`, `targetVersion`, `canApply`, `config`, `conflicts` and `resolved`: `config` is the complete configuration after the choices, `conflicts` holds only the unchosen conflicts with their original details and current values, and `canApply` is true only when `conflicts` is empty. Each `resolved` entry holds only `path` and `choice`: `choice` is the confirmed string for side selections or `"custom"` for every custom selection. Both `conflicts` and `resolved` are sorted by path in Unicode code point order and are always present, even when empty. An invalid or unknown version, invalid store, a configuration violating the existing rules, a non-object decisions value, a non-string key, a key that is not an original conflict path, a choice that is neither a string nor an object, an illegal string choice, or a custom object with a missing field, an extra field, a non-boolean `present`, or a `value` containing a non-string key, a non-finite number, a non-JSON value or a circular reference raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the four files, printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid run prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when conflicts remain. Neither success nor failure modifies the arguments, the input files or the store, or creates any file or directory, and mutating nested values in the returned result never reaches the passed inputs.
28	
29	`ReleaseDesk.apply_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config, expected_config, decisions, current_path)` applies a confirmed plan to a local configuration file, and `python3 release_desk.py apply-config 1.0.0 2.0.0 base.json target.json expected.json decisions.json current.json` reads the base, target and expected configurations plus the decisions from four UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection and treats the fifth path as the write target. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); same-version and reverse-order pairs are allowed, and a missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown. The target file must already exist and must not be a symbolic link, and it must not be the same file as the store or as any of the four input files — textual path aliases and hard links are recognized — with violations raising `ValueError`; a missing target or any read or write failure raises `OSError`, and neither a missing target nor missing directories are ever created. The file is read as UTF-8 JSON under the same whole-file duplicate-key rule as everywhere (encoding, syntax and repeated-key errors raise `ValueError`), validated like any configuration, and compared with the expected snapshot using the existing configuration equality rules; any mismatch raises `ValueError` before anything is written. The change is then processed exactly like `resolve_config`: independent current edits are kept, side selections and custom decisions are accepted, decision keys must be original conflict paths (an empty decisions object is valid when there are no conflicts), and any conflict left undecided raises `ValueError`. The result holds only `baseVersion`, `targetVersion`, `changed`, `config` and `resolved`, where `config` and `resolved` carry the same content and path ordering as the `resolve_config` result and `changed` is true only when the final configuration differs semantically from the read one. When `changed` is true the target is replaced wholesale with UTF-8 JSON ending in a newline; when it is false the target's bytes and modification time are left untouched. With any conflict `canUpdate` is false, `items` is the normalized original checklist unchanged, `updated` is empty, `changed` is false and no partial update is reported; `ready` then reflects the original checklist. A valid preview prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when it reports conflicts; any exception prints only a single-line `error` object with exit 2. Other public entry points keep their existing behavior.
88	
89	`ReleaseDesk.preview_merge_checklist(version, base, incoming, current)` is a read-only three-way merge preview of same-version checklists, and `python3 release_desk.py merge-checklist 1.2.0 base.json incoming.json current.json` reads the common base, the incoming checklist and the current checklist from three UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection. All three inputs follow the existing checklist rules — including the rule that each declared version must equal the queried version — the whole store is validated before the version is looked up (a missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown), and the version must be registered. Items are matched by their normalized ids, case-sensitively after trimming with no Unicode normalization, and compared as whole normalized items: only `id`, `text`, `required` and `status` take part, extra fields are ignored, and a missing item differs from any present one.
90	
91	For each id, an incoming side equal to the base or to the current side keeps the current side; otherwise a current side equal to the base adopts the incoming side; every remaining case is one whole-item conflict that keeps the current side's presence state and content. Additions, deletions and modifications all follow this rule, non-conflicting changes still enter the preview, and item fields are never merged separately. The result holds only `version`, `canMerge`, `ready`, `items` and `conflicts`: `canMerge` is true only when no conflict was reported, and `ready` follows the existing rule that every required item is `done`. `items` carries only the four normalized fields, keeps the current-side item order and then appends, in incoming-side order, the preview items the current side lacks. `conflicts` is always an array, sorted by id in Unicode code point order, each entry holding only `id`, `base`, `incoming` and `current`, the last three being the complete normalized item or `null` when that side lacks the id. A preview that would be empty or would hold no required item raises `ValueError`, and this result validation applies to conflicting previews too.
92	
93	An invalid or unregistered version, a declared-version mismatch, an invalid checklist or store, an empty preview or a preview without any required item raises `ValueError`, while a missing or unreadable file raises `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the three files, printing only a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid preview — conflicts included — prints the single-line result with exit 0. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed payloads, the input files or the store, no file or directory is created, and mutating the returned data never reaches the inputs. Other public entry points keep their existing behavior.
94	
95	`ReleaseDesk.resolve_merge_checklist(version, base, incoming, current, decisions)` is a read-only confirmation layer over `preview_merge_checklist`, and `python3 release_desk.py resolve-merge-checklist 1.2.0 base.json incoming.json current.json decisions.json` reads the three checklists and the decisions from four UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection. The version, checklist, store and version-registration checks follow `merge-checklist` exactly, including validating the whole store first, treating a missing store as empty and then reporting the version as unknown, matching declared versions, comparing whole normalized items, merging non-conflicting changes identically, and requiring both the original preview and the confirmed checklist to be non-empty and to contain at least one required item.
96	
97	`decisions` is a JSON object, possibly empty, mapping original preview conflict ids to either the string `"incoming"` or the string `"current"`; partial selections are allowed. Keys match the normalized conflict ids exactly — case-sensitively, without trimming surrounding whitespace or Unicode normalization — and a key that is not an original conflict id is rejected, as is any non-object decision value, non-string key or choice other than the two strings. Choosing a side adopts that side's complete item; item fields are never merged separately. When the chosen side lacks the id the item is deleted, and choosing a side whose content is unchanged still counts as a confirmed decision. Unchosen conflicts keep their original details (including the current side's presence state and content) and keep the current item in the checklist; their fields are never merged field by field.
98	
99	The result holds only `version`, `canMerge`, `ready`, `items`, `conflicts` and `resolved`. `items` carries only the four normalized fields, follows the current-side item order and then appends, in incoming-side order, items the current side originally lacked; confirmed deletions are absent. `canMerge` is true only when `conflicts` is empty, and `ready` follows the existing rule that every required item is `done`. `conflicts` holds only the unconfirmed conflicts in the preview structure, and each `resolved` entry holds only `id` and the original `choice` string. Both arrays are always present and are sorted by id in Unicode code point order. An invalid or unregistered version, a declared-version mismatch, an invalid checklist or store, a non-object decisions value, a non-string key, a key that is not an original conflict id, an illegal choice, or an empty or required-item-free original preview or confirmed checklist raises `ValueError`, while a missing or unreadable checklist or decisions file raises `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the four files, printing only a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid run prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when conflicts remain. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed objects, the input files or the store, no file or directory is created, and mutating the returned data never reaches the inputs. All other public entry points keep their existing behavior.
100	
101	`ReleaseDesk.apply_merge_checklist(version, base, incoming, expected, decisions, current_path)` saves a confirmed merge to a local checklist file, and `python3 release_desk.py apply-merge-checklist 1.2.0 base.json incoming.json expected.json decisions.json current.json` reads the base, incoming and expected checklists plus the decisions from four UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection and treats the fifth path as the write target. The version, checklist, decisions, store and version-registration checks follow `resolve-merge-checklist` exactly, with the expected checklist validated like every other checklist. The target file must already exist and must not be a symbolic link, and it must not be the same file as the store or as any of the four input files — textual path aliases and hard links are recognized — with violations raising `ValueError`; a missing target or any read or write failure raises `OSError`, and neither a missing target nor missing directories are ever created. The file is read as UTF-8 JSON under the same whole-file duplicate-key rule as everywhere (encoding, syntax and repeated-key errors raise `ValueError`), validated like any checklist, and its declared version and normalized item sequence must equal the expected snapshot: extra fields, object key order and trimmable surrounding whitespace do not take part, item order does, and any mismatch raises `ValueError` before anything is written. The merge then follows `resolve_merge_checklist` exactly — whole-item merging, incoming/current side selections, deletions, ordering and result legality — with the actually read target as the current side; any conflict left undecided raises `ValueError`, an empty decisions object is valid when there are no conflicts, and a not-ready result still saves. The result holds only `version`, `changed`, `items`, `resolved` and `ready`, where `items` and `resolved` carry the same content and ordering as the corresponding `resolve_merge_checklist` result. `changed` is true only when the normalized item sequence differs from the read one; then the target is replaced wholesale with UTF-8 JSON holding only `version` and `items` and ending in a newline, and when it is false the target's bytes and modification time are left untouched. Validation and read or write failures always preserve the target's original bytes and leave no new file or directory behind, and neither success nor failure modifies the passed objects, the input files or the store; mutating the returned data never reaches the inputs. All other public entry points keep their existing behavior.
102

file.content:
# Release Desk

Maintain local release records and generate Markdown notes grouped as Added, Changed and Fixed. Requires Python 3.10+; only the standard library is used.

`python3 release_desk.py notes 1.1.0` renders the included second release. `python3 release_desk.py versions` lists sample versions in numeric order. `samples/next-changes.json` is a candidate change list; to try registration without changing the sample store, use `python3 release_desk.py --store .state/releases.json add 1.2.0 samples/next-changes.json` and query that same store.

Version identifiers have exactly three nonnegative numeric components, without prefixes, prerelease suffixes or leading zeros. Each release has at least one single-line change with a recognized category. Existing versions cannot be replaced. Category order is fixed and the input order within a category is retained. This version does not inspect Git or publish packages.

`python3 release_desk.py diff 1.0.0 1.1.0` compares two registered versions in the same store and prints a single-line JSON object with `baseVersion`, `targetVersion` and the `added`, `removed` and `unchanged` entries of the target relative to the base. Entries match on category plus trimmed, case-sensitive text; duplicates pair up by occurrence. Comparing a version with itself or a higher with a lower version is allowed. The comparison is read-only and never infers actual product changes.

`ReleaseDesk.diff_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config)` is a read-only structural comparison of two externally supplied JSON configuration objects, and `python3 release_desk.py diff-config 1.0.0 1.1.0 base.json target.json` reads both configurations from UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); comparing a version with itself or a higher with a lower version is allowed. The configurations come solely from the arguments or files — they are never written to the store and never inferred from change entries — and neither the passed objects, the files nor the store are modified, and no directory is created.

Each root configuration must be a JSON object. When the same field exists in both and both values are objects, comparison descends recursively; otherwise the complete values are compared. Arrays are never split: they compare as whole values and element order is significant, with objects inside arrays following the same object rules. A field or whole subobject present only in the target yields one `added` entry, one present only in the base yields one `removed` entry, both carrying `path` and `value`; a field present on both sides with differing values yields a `changed` entry carrying `path`, `before` (the base value) and `after` (the target value). All three arrays are always present, and identical configurations return three empty arrays. `path` is a JSON Pointer rooted at the empty string (`/a/b`, `/` for an empty field name), with `~` and `/` in field names escaped as `~0` and `~1`. Each array is sorted by path in Unicode code point order; key matching is case-sensitive with no Unicode normalization and empty key names are allowed. Booleans differ from numbers even when comparing `true` with `1`, numerically equal integers and floats compare equal, `null` differs from a missing field, and object key order is ignored.

An invalid or unknown version, invalid store content, a non-object root, a non-string key, a non-JSON value (including non-finite numbers) or a circular reference raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects encoding errors, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level (the same whole-file duplicate-key rule as everywhere), printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2 for any of these and the single-line result with exit 0 on success. A missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown.

`ReleaseDesk.preview_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config, current_config)` is a read-only three-way preview that checks whether applying the base→target plan would overwrite independent edits already present in the current configuration, and `python3 release_desk.py preview-config 1.0.0 2.0.0 base.json target.json current.json` reads all three configurations from UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); same-version and reverse-order pairs are allowed, just like `diff-config`. The configurations come solely from the arguments or files and follow the same validation, equality, pointer and key rules as `diff_config`, and nothing — the passed objects, the files, the store — is modified and no directory is created.

For each field, the plan is the base→target change. A field the plan does not change keeps its current presence state and value, including independent current edits and current-only fields. When the plan does change a field, a current value equal to the target is kept, a current state equal to the base adopts the target (whole additions and deletions included), and any other state is resolved field by field only when the field exists on all three sides and all three values are objects; otherwise it is one conflict at that path whose preview keeps the current field's presence state and value. Whole subobject additions and deletions, arrays (never split) and type changes are always judged as a whole, so a whole-value conflict never lists subpaths; every other non-conflicting change still enters the preview. Equality uses the `diff_config` rules, including `null` differing from a missing field and two missing fields being equal. The result holds only `baseVersion`, `targetVersion`, `canApply`, `config` and `conflicts`: `config` is the complete previewed object, `canApply` is true only when `conflicts` is empty, and each conflict holds only `path` plus `base`, `target` and `current`, each of those holding a `present` boolean and a `value` only when present. `path` uses the same JSON Pointer escaping as `diff-config`, and `conflicts` is sorted by path in Unicode code point order. For example, a target that changes the port while the current config only changes a timeout keeps both changes, while both sides changing the same port to different values keeps the current port and reports a `/port` conflict.

An invalid or unknown version, invalid store or a configuration violating the existing config validation rules raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects encoding errors, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the three files, printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid preview prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when it reports conflicts, and a missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown. Neither success nor failure modifies the arguments, the input files or the store, or creates any file or directory.

`ReleaseDesk.resolve_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config, current_config, decisions)` is a read-only confirmation layer over `preview_config`, and `python3 release_desk.py resolve-config 1.0.0 2.0.0 base.json target.json current.json decisions.json` reads the three configurations and the decisions from four UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); same-version and reverse-order pairs are allowed, and the configurations come solely from the arguments or files under the same validation, equality, pointer and key rules as `preview_config`. `decisions` is a JSON object, possibly empty, mapping original `preview_config` conflict paths to either the string `"target"`, the string `"current"` or a custom decision object; strings and custom objects may be mixed freely in the same map. Keys match verbatim using the same JSON Pointer escaping (`~0`, `~1`), with no trimming or Unicode normalization; only whole conflict paths are accepted — arrays, type changes and whole-object conflicts cannot be decided at subpaths, and non-conflict fields are rejected — and partial selections are allowed. Choosing `"target"` adopts that conflict's complete target-side presence state and value; choosing `"current"` keeps the current side and records the conflict as handled. When the chosen side is missing the field is deleted, and a `null` side value is kept as a value rather than treated as missing. Every other non-conflicting change and every independent current edit keeps its preview result.

A custom decision object holds a strict boolean `present`. When `present` is true the object holds exactly `present` and a required `value`; when `present` is false it holds exactly `present` and the field is deleted. `value` accepts any legal JSON value, including `null`, arrays and objects. The custom value replaces the selected field wholesale: objects, arrays and type changes are never recursively merged, and a value numerically or structurally equal to the target or current side still counts as a custom, handled decision. Every other non-conflicting change and every independent current edit keeps its preview result. For example, when the port is 80 on the base side, 8080 on the target side and 9000 on the current side, a `{"present": true, "value": 9001}` decision on `/port` confirms 9001 while an independently modified timeout keeps its current value.

The result holds only `baseVersion`, `targetVersion`, `canApply`, `config`, `conflicts` and `resolved`: `config` is the complete configuration after the choices, `conflicts` holds only the unchosen conflicts with their original details and current values, and `canApply` is true only when `conflicts` is empty. Each `resolved` entry holds only `path` and `choice`: `choice` is the confirmed string for side selections or `"custom"` for every custom selection. Both `conflicts` and `resolved` are sorted by path in Unicode code point order and are always present, even when empty. An invalid or unknown version, invalid store, a configuration violating the existing rules, a non-object decisions value, a non-string key, a key that is not an original conflict path, a choice that is neither a string nor an object, an illegal string choice, or a custom object with a missing field, an extra field, a non-boolean `present`, or a `value` containing a non-string key, a non-finite number, a non-JSON value or a circular reference raises `ValueError`, while unreadable files raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the four files, printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid run prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when conflicts remain. Neither success nor failure modifies the arguments, the input files or the store, or creates any file or directory, and mutating nested values in the returned result never reaches the passed inputs.

`ReleaseDesk.apply_config(base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config, expected_config, decisions, current_path)` applies a confirmed plan to a local configuration file, and `python3 release_desk.py apply-config 1.0.0 2.0.0 base.json target.json expected.json decisions.json current.json` reads the base, target and expected configurations plus the decisions from four UTF-8 JSON files using the same `--store` selection and treats the fifth path as the write target. Both versions must already be registered (the whole store is validated first); same-version and reverse-order pairs are allowed, and a missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown. The target file must already exist and must not be a symbolic link, and it must not be the same file as the store or as any of the four input files — textual path aliases and hard links are recognized — with violations raising `ValueError`; a missing target or any read or write failure raises `OSError`, and neither a missing target nor missing directories are ever created. The file is read as UTF-8 JSON under the same whole-file duplicate-key rule as everywhere (encoding, syntax and repeated-key errors raise `ValueError`), validated like any configuration, and compared with the expected snapshot using the existing configuration equality rules; any mismatch raises `ValueError` before anything is written. The change is then processed exactly like `resolve_config`: independent current edits are kept, side selections and custom decisions are accepted, decision keys must be original conflict paths (an empty decisions object is valid when there are no conflicts), and any conflict left undecided raises `ValueError`. The result holds only `baseVersion`, `targetVersion`, `changed`, `config` and `resolved`, where `config` and `resolved` carry the same content and path ordering as the `resolve_config` result and `changed` is true only when the final configuration differs semantically from the read one. When `changed` is true the target is replaced wholesale with UTF-8 JSON ending in a newline; when it is false the target's bytes and modification time are left untouched. Validation and read or write failures always preserve the target's original bytes, and neither success nor failure modifies the passed objects, the four input files or the store.

The API is `ReleaseDesk.add`, `versions`, `notes`, `diff`, `diff_config`, `preview_config`, `resolve_config`, `apply_config`, `import_releases`, `preview_import_releases`, `export_releases`, `checklist`, `check_dependencies`, `explain_dependencies`, `generate_checklist`, `audit_checklist`, `release_record`, `release_record_with_dependencies`, `reconcile_checklist`, `migrate_checklist`, `update_checklist`, `preview_update_checklist`, `preview_merge_checklist` and `resolve_merge_checklist`. JSON is used for command results and errors except `notes`, which prints Markdown. Invalid input or file errors exit 2. Run `python3 -B -m unittest -v` for rendering, sorting, validation, diff, config diff, config preview, config resolution, config apply, import, preview, export, checklist, dependency checks, dependency explanations, template filtering, audit, merge preview, merge resolution and CLI tests.

Every JSON file read from disk — the store, the `add` changes file and the `import` batch file — is rejected as a whole when any single object repeats a key, failing with `duplicate JSON object key` before anything is registered or written. Keys are compared exactly as decoded: case-sensitively, without trimming or Unicode normalization, so a key spelled with `\u` escapes still collides with its plain spelling. Identical change entries in an array remain legal.

`python3 release_desk.py import batches.json` merges multiple releases from a local JSON file that maps versions to change arrays, using the same validation as `add` and the `--store` target. It prints a single-line JSON object with numerically sorted `imported` and `skipped` arrays: an existing version is skipped only when its normalized categories, texts and order match exactly, and any count, order, category or text difference is a conflict that aborts the whole import. An empty object is valid and changes nothing; a missing target store is treated as empty and is not created when every release is skipped. Validation, conflicts and file errors leave any existing store byte-for-byte untouched. The import never reads Git or publishes packages.

`python3 release_desk.py import --dry-run batches.json` previews the same batch without writing anything. It prints a single-line JSON object with numerically sorted `imported` and `skipped` arrays, a `conflicts` array sorted the same way, and `canImport`, which is true only when no version conflicts. Each conflict detail carries `version` plus the `added`, `removed` and `unchanged` entries of the batch relative to the stored release, classified exactly like `diff` (fixed category order, trimmed case-sensitive texts, duplicates paired by occurrence, entries holding only `category` and `text`), and `orderOnly`, which is true only when the stored and batch arrays differ solely in entry order. Conflicts still exit 0 in preview mode, while an invalid batch, store or unreadable file fails with an `error` object and exit 2. The preview validates the whole store even for an empty batch, treats a missing store as empty, and never creates or modifies the store, its parent directories, the batch file or the passed payload. `ReleaseDesk.preview_import_releases(payload)` offers the same preview directly, raising `ValueError` on invalid batch or store content and `OSError` on read failures.

`python3 release_desk.py export` prints a single-line JSON object mapping versions to change arrays, exactly in the shape accepted by `import`: versions are sorted by numeric components and each entry contains only `category` and trimmed `text`, preserving the original array order, repeated entries and Chinese text as-is. Exporting without `--version` includes every release; repeated `--version` filters may be passed and duplicates are only kept once. A missing store is treated as an empty object and is never created, while selecting a version from an empty store fails as an unknown release. The whole store is validated regardless of selection, and exporting never modifies it; importing an export into an empty store imports every release, and importing it again skips every release.

With `--output file.json` the object is written as UTF-8 JSON ending in a newline, creating missing parent directories and replacing any existing file wholesale, and the command instead prints a single-line object whose `exported` value is the numerically sorted array of exported versions. Validation or write failures leave an existing target byte-for-byte untouched and never create a missing target. The output must not point at the store file, including textual path aliases, symlinks and hard links; doing so fails like any other invalid input.

`ReleaseDesk.checklist(version, payload)` is a read-only release readiness check, and `python3 release_desk.py check 1.2.0 checklist.json` runs it against a UTF-8 JSON file using the same `--store` selection. The checklist object holds `version` and `items`: the version follows the existing version rules and must equal the queried version, and `items` is a non-empty array containing at least one required check. Each item has `id`, `text`, `required` and `status` only; `id` and `text` are strings that are non-empty after trimming surrounding whitespace and are rejected when the raw value contains a carriage return or newline, `required` is a strict boolean, and `status` is one of `done`, `pending` or `blocked`. Normalized ids must be unique case-sensitively after trimming, with no Unicode normalization (`café` with U+00E9 differs from `caf` + `e` + U+0301), while duplicate item texts are legal. Extra object fields are ignored.

The command prints the same single-line report as the API, holding only `version`, `ready`, `done`, `pending` and `blocked`. The last three arrays group items by declared status, preserving the input order within each group, and each entry holds only the trimmed `id` and `text` plus the original `required` and `status`. `ready` is true only when every required item is `done`; unfinished or blocked optional items stay in their groups but never affect readiness. Status comes solely from the checklist — nothing is inferred from change texts. An invalid version, checklist structure or field, duplicate id, version mismatch, unknown release or invalid store content raises `ValueError`, and read failures raise `OSError`; the CLI reports these, plus non-UTF-8 or malformed JSON checklist files, as a single-line `error` object with exit 2, while a valid checklist prints its report with exit 0 regardless of readiness. The checklist file follows the same duplicate-JSON-key whole-file rejection rule. The whole store is validated, a missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown, and neither success nor failure modifies the store, the checklist file or the passed payload, or creates any file or directory.

`ReleaseDesk.check_dependencies(version, checklist, dependencies)` is a read-only dependency-aware variant of `checklist`, and `python3 release_desk.py check-dependencies 1.2.0 checklist.json dependencies.json` reads the checklist and a dependency map from two UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection. The version, checklist and complete store checks follow `checklist` exactly — the declared checklist version must equal the queried version, the whole store is validated first, and a missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown. The dependency value is a JSON object, possibly empty, that maps an item id to the array of its direct prerequisite ids; an empty array and an omitted item both mean "no prerequisites". Every id on either end follows the checklist single-line id rule: a string non-empty after trimming surrounding whitespace, rejected when the raw value contains a carriage return or newline, matched case-sensitively after trimming with no Unicode normalization. Every array value must be an array, prerequisite ids must be unique within one array after normalization, normalized object keys must be unique, both ends must reference checklist items, and a self dependency or any cycle — even a cycle involving only optional items — is rejected. The dependency file follows the same duplicate-JSON-key whole-file rejection rule as every other file.

The report holds only `version`, `ready` and `items`. `items` keeps the checklist order, and each item carries the normalized `id`, `text`, `required` and the original declared `status`, plus `effectiveStatus` and `waiting`. `effectiveStatus` is `"blocked"` when any direct prerequisite is not effectively `done`, no matter what the item declared; otherwise it equals the declared status. Blocking propagates layer by layer: when A depends on B and B depends on C, with A and B declared `done` and C `pending`, both A and B are effectively blocked, while A's `waiting` lists only B. `waiting` is always an array and lists, in dependency-array order, only the direct prerequisites whose effective status is not `done`; transitive prerequisites are never listed. `ready` is true only when every required item is effectively `done`; optional items never decide readiness themselves, but an optional prerequisite that is not effectively done still blocks a required item that depends on it. With no dependencies the report's readiness is identical to `check`. An invalid or unknown version, a version mismatch, an invalid checklist or store, a non-object dependency value, an illegal id, a normalized duplicate key or duplicate array id, a non-array dependency value, a reference to an unknown item at either end, a self dependency or a cycle raises `ValueError`, and read failures raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in either file, printing only a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid run prints the single-line report with exit 0 even when it is not ready. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed objects, the input files or the store, or creates any file or directory, and mutating the returned data never reaches the inputs. All other public entry points keep their existing behavior.

`ReleaseDesk.explain_dependencies(version, checklist, dependencies)` is a read-only release-blocker explanation layered on `check_dependencies`, and `python3 release_desk.py explain-dependencies 1.2.0 checklist.json dependencies.json` reads the checklist and the dependency map from two UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection. Input normalization, validation, effective statuses and the readiness rule follow `check_dependencies` exactly — the declared checklist version must equal the queried version, the whole store is validated first, a missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown, and statuses still come solely from the checklist.

The report holds only `version`, `ready` and `reasons`. For every required item whose effective status is not `done`, the explanation traces from the item itself, following only prerequisites whose effective status is not `done`. Every reached node declared `pending` or `blocked` counts as a reason and its own prerequisites are still traced; nodes declared `done` only carry the path. Optional items that affect no required item never appear. `reasons` lists each reason once, in checklist order, holding only the normalized `id`, `text`, `required`, declared `status` and `affected`. `affected` lists each affected required item once, in checklist order, holding only `id` and `path`, where `path` is the id array from the required item to the reason, both ends included — a reason that is the required item itself has a one-id path. For one required-item/reason pair the path with the fewest edges is chosen; equal-length paths are compared node by node by checklist position and the path with the smaller first differing position wins, regardless of dependency-array order. When `ready` is true, `reasons` is an empty array. For example, with required A and optional B declared `done`, A depending on B and B depending on pending C, only C is listed as a reason and its `affected` holds A with path `["A", "B", "C"]`. An invalid or unknown version, a version mismatch, an invalid checklist, dependency map or store raises `ValueError`, and read failures raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in either file, printing only a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid run prints the single-line report with exit 0 even when it is not ready. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed objects, the input files or the store, or creates any file or directory, and mutating the returned data never reaches the inputs. All other public entry points keep their existing behavior.

class CheckDependenciesTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT)
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.path = Path(self.temp.name) / "releases.json"
        self.desk = ReleaseDesk(self.path)
        self.desk.add("1.2.0", [{"category": "Added", "text": "One"}])

    def payload(self, *items):
        if not items:
            items = (
                {"id": "a", "text": "A", "required": True, "status": "done"},
                {"id": "b", "text": "B", "required": True, "status": "done"},
                {"id": "c", "text": "C", "required": False, "status": "pending"},
            )
        return {"version": "1.2.0", "items": list(items)}

    def test_no_dependencies_matches_check(self):
        for dependencies in ({}, {"a": [], "b": [], "c": []}):
            report = self.desk.check_dependencies("1.2.0", self.payload(), dependencies)
            self.assertEqual(set(report), {"version", "ready", "items"})
            self.assertTrue(report["ready"])
            self.assertEqual([item["id"] for item in report["items"]], ["a", "b", "c"])
            for item in report["items"]:
                self.assertEqual(set(item),
                                 {"id", "text", "required", "status", "effectiveStatus", "waiting"})
                self.assertEqual(item["effectiveStatus"], item["status"])
                self.assertEqual(item["waiting"], [])

    def test_chain_blocks_layer_by_layer_with_direct_only_waiting(self):
        # The spec example: A depends on B, B on C; A and B declare done while
        # C is pending. Both are blocked effectively, and A waits only on B.
        payload = self.payload()
        report = self.desk.check_dependencies("1.2.0", payload, {"a": ["b"], "b": ["c"]})
        effects = {item["id"]: item for item in report["items"]}
        self.assertFalse(report["ready"])
        self.assertEqual(effects["a"]["status"], "done")
        self.assertEqual(effects["a"]["effectiveStatus"], "blocked")
        self.assertEqual(effects["a"]["waiting"], ["b"])
        self.assertEqual(effects["b"]["effectiveStatus"], "blocked")
        self.assertEqual(effects["b"]["waiting"], ["c"])
        self.assertEqual(effects["c"]["effectiveStatus"], "pending")
        self.assertEqual(effects["c"]["waiting"], [])

    def test_undone_prerequisite_blocks_any_declared_status(self):
        payload = self.payload(
            {"id": "a", "text": "A", "required": True, "status": "pending"},
            {"id": "b", "text": "B", "required": True, "status": "blocked"},
            {"id": "c", "text": "C", "required": False, "status": "pending"},
        )
        report = self.desk.check_dependencies("1.2.0", payload, {"a": ["c"], "b": ["c"]})
        effects = {item["id"]: item["effectiveStatus"] for item in report["items"]}
        self.assertEqual(effects, {"a": "blocked", "b": "blocked", "c": "pending"})

    def test_waiting_lists_only_not_done_direct_prerequisites_in_array_order(self):
        payload = self.payload(
            {"id": "a", "text": "A", "required": True, "status": "done"},
            {"id": "b", "text": "B", "required": False, "status": "done"},
            {"id": "c", "text": "C", "required": False, "status": "pending"},
            {"id": "d", "text": "D", "required": False, "status": "blocked"},
        )
        deps = {"a": ["b", "c", "d"]}
        report = self.desk.check_dependencies("1.2.0", payload, deps)
        item_a = report["items"][0]
        # b is effectively done and drops out; waiting keeps only the not-done
        # direct prerequisites in dependency-array order, never transitive ones.
        self.assertEqual(item_a["waiting"], ["c", "d"])
        self.assertEqual(item_a["effectiveStatus"], "blocked")

    def test_optional_items_and_readiness(self):
        # A blocked optional item never decides readiness on its own...
        optional_blocked = self.payload(
            {"id": "a", "text": "A", "required": True, "status": "done"},
            {"id": "b", "text": "B", "required": False, "status": "pending"},
